taskDescription: Drag the words into the correct boxes
resetDropDescription: Are you sure you want to reset this drop zone?
a11yCheck: Check the answers. The responses will be marked as correct, incorrect, or unanswered.
a11yShowSolution: Show the solution. The task will be marked with its correct solution.
a11yRetry: Retry the task. Reset all responses and start the task over again.
textField:
In Scratch, you can use a *conditional* loop to make a cat keep walking forward until it bumps into a wall.
To make a game character keep trying a task until the player gets it right, we use the *repeat until* block.
If you use a *forever* block by mistake, your character will never stop moving, and you will not be able to program further actions.
The code blocks placed inside the loop are called the loop *body*, and they will keep running until the stopping rule is reached.
To safely explore a dark maze, you can program your robot to repeat moving forward until it is touching a *wall*.
A conditional loop keeps checking the rule over and over to see if the stopping condition is *true* yet.
